newsitem.title: GERMANY: Firm dollar helps boost N.Europe rapeseed price.
newsitem.headline: Firm dollar helps boost N.Europe rapeseed price.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in Northern Europe firmed along with the stronger dollar which has raised soybean prices versus EU currencies, brokers said on Friday.

New crop buyers for ex-harvest rapeseed raised offers by five marks on the week to 437.50 per tonne free Hamburg. Rapeseed prices for delivery at points other than Hamburg were in a broadly steady 420-435 marks range for July.
November rapeseed on the Matif futures traded at 441 marks, off one from Thursday's close and unchanged from last week.
Nearby prices were expected to ease under harvest pressure over the next few weeks but harvesting efforts for the time being were scuppered by heavy rainfall in south eastern and southern Germany.
This hampered ex-harvest sales, although crushers and traders were enquiring for material.
The harvest in the country's north will start next week.
Yields in eastern Germany so far are between three and four tonnes per hectare (tph) compared with the extremely weak 1997 pan-German result of 2.28 tph last year.

In products, Aug/Oct rape meal was up 0.25 marks/100 kg at 23.00 and Nov/Jan steady at 24.50. Rape oil sellers prices were off one mark at 91.75 marks for August while Sept/Oct was off 0.50 at 93.00 marks.
